title: Review Standard: One Cleaning and Damage Fees Assessment per Trip
content:
**Clause 1.** A rider may have any number of Cleaning and Damage Fees assessments over time, but a trip carries at most the maximum number of assessments per trip set for the fee level, which is one assessment.

**Clause 2.** A report is accepted only when the trip has no other assessment in reported, under review, charged, disputed, upheld or reversed status; when an earlier report on the trip was denied, a new report is not opened and the driver uses reconsideration of the denied one instead.

**Clause 3.** A mess and damage found on the same trip are reported as one assessment at the higher level that the evidence supports.

## Basis of the check

- The check rests on the system record: the assessments already registered against the same trip and the status each one holds at the time of the new report. What the driver or the rider says about an earlier report does not replace that record.
- The object of the check is the trip: assessments are compared by the trip they were raised on, whichever rider they are against and whichever level they hold.
- Each report is its own record, told apart by the moment it was registered; a second report on the same trip is a separate record, not an update of the first.

## Status of an earlier assessment on the same trip

| Status of the earlier assessment | Effect on a new report on that trip |
|---|---|
| reported | not accepted |
| under review | not accepted |
| charged | not accepted |
| disputed | not accepted |
| upheld | not accepted |
| reversed | not accepted |
| denied | a new report is not opened; the driver uses reconsideration of the denied report |

## Illustrations (hypothetical)

- A trip already carries an assessment whose fee was reversed in full after a dispute. A new report on that trip is not accepted: reversed is one of the statuses that blocks it.
- A driver finds a drink spilled across a seat and a cracked interior trim panel on the same trip. Both are reported as one assessment, at the higher of the levels the evidence supports.
- A driver's earlier report on a trip was denied. The driver does not open a new report on the trip; the denied report is the one taken back through reconsideration.
